add.title: Keepin’ It “Real”: Israel’s Segregation of Transgender Prisoners and the Transgender/Cisgender Binary (Lihi Yona, Buffalo Journal of Gender, Law & Social Policy, Vol. 24, p. 43)
add.summary: Law-journal article documenting that Israel’s response to transgender prisoners’ vulnerability has been to isolate/segragate them, keeping trans inmates apart from the rest of the prison population rather than placing them in facilities matching their gender identity. Establishes that a trans prisoner faces isolation-based custody as the default management practice.

add.title: New Israel Fund – Victory for Transgender Rights in Israeli Prisons
add.summary: October 2019 precedent-setting case: an Israeli court ordered the Israel Prison Service to provide hormone-replacement therapy to a trans woman prisoner and transfer her from a male prison to a female one, after ACRI petitioned. The prisoner was initially placed in a separate wing of the women’s prison, and ACRI prepared a further petition to have her housed with the general population — showing case-by-case placement review by the courts, and that trans women have at times been held in men’s prisons in Israel.
